concept: Planner plan scoring and EOF bonus
summary: Source-anchored research for Planner plan scoring and EOF bonus. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: In current MongoDB plan_ranker_util.h, pickBestPlan() sets eofBonus to 1 and adds that point when the candidate root statistics report common.isEOF. The code comment says multiple candidates that hit EOF during the same round-robin calls also receive the bonus. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A trial sample can mis-rank plans when index order and predicate values are correlated: MongoDB issue SERVER-20616 describes a range scan that looks productive on the early sample, and an arXiv study (Tao et al., 2024) found MongoDB 7.0.1 could prefer index scans over faster collection scans, with more than twice the optimal runtime in some cases. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-20616 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2409.16544v1

The EOF formula describes the classic multi-planner path, not every eligible query choice: the current manual says multi-planning with a cost-based ranker backup is the default plan-selection mechanism for eligible queries starting in MongoDB 8.3, and the backup may evaluate plans when the initial trial is unsuccessful. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A University of Sydney study evaluated FPTP on MongoDB 7.0.1 using simple two-range query families. It found cases where the optimizer chose index scans even though collection scans ran faster, and argued that advanced-per-work scoring can undercount index access plus document-fetch cost. The study does not isolate EOF bonus as the cause of every misranking. (medium confidence)

In the classic multi-planner, hitting EOF is a distinct way for the trial to end, separate from a candidate reaching the result-count limit: the first plan to hit EOF wins automatically and the other plans stop being evaluated. EOF means all documents from the plan have been retrieved. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.2/src/mongo/db/exec/multi_plan.cpp ; https://arxiv.org/html/2409.16544v1

The productivity score is not elapsed time: MongoDB's Jira describes work as an artificial unit that proxies CPU + IO time, and the classic multi-planner's winner is the plan producing the most results during the trial while performing the least work. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-20616 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md

A Nov 2025 example by Franck Pachot reports candidate scores of 2.012, 1.010, and 1.007; the first candidate’s one-point lead mostly comes from reaching EOF during the trial. This illustrates how trial completion can dominate small productivity differences, but it is one query example rather than a general performance result. (medium confidence)

In the current classic ranker, a candidate's basic score starts at 1 and adds root productivity (advanced divided by works) plus small tie-breaker bonuses that favor avoiding fetch, blocking sort, and index-intersection stages; some query shapes have additional score adjustments. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/plan_ranker.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/plan_ranker.cpp

In the classic plan ranker, a candidate's score is baseScore (1) + productivity (advanced / works) + tieBreakers, and the highest score wins. Releases such as 8.2.2 and 7.0.1 also add an eofBonus (1.0) when a plan hits EOF during the trial. In current master, plan_ranker.h computes score = baseScore + productivity + tieBreakers + groupByDistinctBonus, with no eofBonus term. The cited classic_runtime_planner README does not state this formula. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/plan_ranker.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/plan_ranker.cpp ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r8.2.2/src/mongo/db/query/plan_ranker_util.h ; https://arxiv.org/html/2409.16544v1

MongoDB’s current PlanScorer base class leaves the productivity calculation to concrete scorer implementations. The classic README’s advanced / works formula should not be assumed to describe every execution engine or ranking path. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
